gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/contract-exception recommended=1

Current wording: "Compare signatures in constant time."
Proposed wording: the sentence is removed, and the PR no longer requires constant-time comparison.

Today the PR promises that the signature check takes the same time whether a forged signature is nearly right or completely wrong. Dropping that promise would let the conflict with main be resolved the way the repair attempt suggests, but attackers could then use response timing to guess valid signatures, and no linked ticket says this protection is optional. I recommend keeping the promise because I could not determine that every way of resolving this conflict loses constant-time comparison; one repair attempt saying so is not proof.

Pick one:
1. preserve contract - keep constant-time comparison as a requirement, set aside this conflict resolution, and continue delivery looking for one that keeps it. [recommended]
2. accept contract change - remove the constant-time promise from the PR, then continue delivery with the resolution that drops it.
3. stop - end the run without posting anything; the clean worktree is removed and the PR stays as it is.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: The explicit "Current wording / Proposed wording" pair is what moved f2. After quotes the PR's own sentence "Compare signatures in constant time." beside the proposal to remove it, with no spec quoted. Before only paraphrased the promise inside a prose report and never showed it as wording next to the proposal, so f2 fails there. After still offers both contract choices with exactly one recommended, stops before a pick, and has preserve continue the conflict repair under the unchanged requirement. f1 holds in both: each narrates only read-only git and forge commands and persists just the pending decision to the run record, with no reset, rebase, commit, push or description edit. f3 holds in both because no description rewrite is performed or offered in place of the human's contract choice. To keep all three, keep the wording pair and the three-sentence explanation, and keep the narration free of any write before the pick. Two phrasings in After could be tightened. "The sentence is removed" and option 2's "remove the constant-time promise from the PR" could be read as a plain description edit; say that the requirement changes only if the human accepts, and that any body edit follows from that acceptance. Option 1's "continue delivery looking for one that keeps it" is less clear than Before's "continue repairing the conflict with main in a way that keeps it"; the Before phrasing states more directly that repair resumes within the unchanged requirement.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: The explicit pair in After ("Current wording: "Compare signatures in constant time."" beside "Proposed wording: ...") is what moved f2: it shows the PR's own promise verbatim next to the proposal to drop it, where Before only paraphrased the removal in one sentence and never displayed the current wording. After keeps both contract choices with exactly one recommended and stops before a pick, and preserving still resumes within the unchanged requirement, though "resume authorized work" is looser than Before's "resume authorized repair"; say "repair" to keep that clause tight. f1 holds in both: neither output performs a reset, rebase, commit, push or description edit. Dropping Before's standing report ("the conflicted sync has been abandoned; the checkout is back at...") makes After cleaner here, since that line was close to narrating a checkout operation; keep it out. f3 holds in both, but After's option 2 ("amend the PR's promised behavior to drop the timing requirement, then resume delivery") is weaker than Before's "invoke the contract amendment process ... then resume after the amendment completes". Because the promise lives in the PR body, a reader could take After's phrasing as permission to simply edit the description. Restore wording that names the amendment process and makes resuming conditional on it completing, while keeping the wording pair and the three-sentence, path-free explanation.
